newsitem.title: UK: Antofagasta to make 120 mln stg placing.
newsitem.headline: Antofagasta to make 120 mln stg placing.

text.p: London-listed Antofagasta Holdings Plc said on Thursday it was making a placing and open offer to raise 120 million stg, of which 62.3 percent was being taken up by the principal shareholder.

The group confirmed it had entered a conditional agreement with two consortia of Japanese companies to dispose of its 40 percent interest in the Minera Los Pelambres copper mine in Chile for around $256 million.
The proposed disposal is for 29.26 million stock units at 415 pence per unit. The placing and open offer is being made to shareholders on the basis of two stock units for every 11 shares.
The placing and open offer is underwritten by HSBC Samuel Montagu except for the 18.24 million stock units for which irrevocable undertakings have been made.
"These proposals, together with debt finance, will provide Antofagasta with the funding required to develop the Los Pelambres project," the company said in a statement.
The first consortium, which plans to buy a 25 percent stake, includes Nippon Mining & Metals Co Ltd, Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd.
The second group, which will hold a 15 percent stake, includes Mitsubishi Materials Corp and Mitsubishi Corp.

Antofagasta said the benefits from the proposals to the company include: unlocking the value of one of its key assets; retaining a controlling interest in one of the world's largest copper mines; and the creation of a strong joint venture to develop Los Pelambres.
It will provide long term off-take contracts for the mine of 400,000 tonnes a year of copper concentrates, helping the firm realise its strategy to become one of the world's biggest copper producers.
Antofagasta is owned by Chile's Luksic group.
